summary: Legacy ASP.NET WebForms 2.0 application (VB.NET) on entirely end-of-life infrastructure. No cloud-native patterns, no containerization, no CI/CD, no managed services, and critical security vulnerabilities. Complete ground-up modernization required across all seven pathways.

findings.title: No cloud-native architecture patterns
findings.description: Monolithic single-page WebForms app with tightly coupled UI, business logic, and data access in a single code-behind file. No separation of concerns, no dependency injection, no service layer.
evidence: Timesheet.aspx.vb: All logic in a single Page class with no abstraction layers

findings.title: In-process session state prevents horizontal scaling
findings.description: Session state is configured as InProc (single-server only). The application cannot run on multiple instances without session loss.
evidence: web.config: sessionState mode="InProc" timeout="60"

findings.title: No health check or readiness endpoints
findings.description: No mechanism for orchestrators or load balancers to determine application health.
evidence: No health check endpoints in any source file

findings.title: ViewState-dependent page lifecycle
findings.description: Multi-megabyte ViewState ties the application to server-affinity and prevents stateless operation.
evidence: README.md documents ViewState bloat making pages multi-megabyte

findings.title: No Dockerfile or container configuration
findings.description: No container artifacts exist in the repository. The application has never been containerized.
evidence: No Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, or .dockerignore in repository

findings.title: Requires full Windows/.NET Framework runtime
findings.description: .NET Framework 2.0 WebForms cannot run in a Linux container. A rewrite to .NET 8+ is required before Linux containerization is viable.
evidence: Application targets .NET Framework 2.0 which requires Windows Server with IIS

findings.title: No container orchestration manifests
findings.description: No Kubernetes manifests, ECS task definitions, or docker-compose files exist.
evidence: No k8s/, kubernetes/, or ecs/ directories in repository

findings.title: Locked into proprietary Microsoft stack
findings.description: The application depends entirely on proprietary technologies: .NET Framework 2.0 (Windows-only), IIS 6, SQL Server 2005, VB.NET. No open-source frameworks or libraries are used.
evidence: web.config: System.Data.SqlClient provider
No open-source library references

findings.title: No cross-platform runtime support
findings.description: .NET Framework 2.0 is Windows-exclusive. The application cannot run on Linux or macOS without a complete rewrite.
evidence: Deployment target is IIS 6 on Windows Server 2003

findings.title: Self-managed SQL Server 2005 on-premises
findings.description: Database runs on an internal server (10.0.6.15) with no managed service, no automated backups, no high availability, and no patching. SQL Server 2005 is end-of-life.
evidence: web.config: Data Source=10.0.6.15;Initial Catalog=Timesheets

findings.title: Raw SQL with string concatenation (SQL injection)
findings.description: Data access uses direct SqlClient with string-concatenated queries, creating critical SQL injection vulnerabilities.
evidence: Timesheet.aspx.vb: "SELECT ... WHERE employee_id = '" & empId & "'"
Timesheet.aspx.vb: "INSERT INTO timesheets ... VALUES ('" & Session("EmployeeId") & "'..."

findings.title: Plaintext credentials in source control
findings.description: Database connection string with password is hardcoded in web.config and committed to the repository.
evidence: web.config: Password=Time2006! in connection string

findings.title: No analytics or reporting capabilities
findings.description: The application only performs basic CRUD on timesheet entries. No reporting views, dashboards, data exports, or analytical queries.
evidence: Timesheet.aspx.vb: Only SELECT and INSERT operations on a single table

findings.title: No event streaming or data pipeline
findings.description: No mechanism to stream timesheet data to analytics systems. All data remains locked in the operational database.
evidence: No event bus, message queue, or change data capture configuration

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline
findings.description: Deployment is a manual Publish from Visual Studio 2005 to a network share. No automated build, test, or deployment process exists.
evidence: No .github/workflows/, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or CI/CD configuration
README.md: Publish from Visual Studio 2005 to a network share

findings.title: No automated testing
findings.description: No test files, no testing framework, no test configuration exists anywhere in the repository.
evidence: No *Test*, *_test*, *.test.*, or *Spec* files in repository

findings.title: No infrastructure as code
findings.description: No Terraform, CDK, CloudFormation, or any IaC templates. Infrastructure is manually provisioned.
evidence: No terraform/, cdk/, cloudformation/, or IaC templates in repository

findings.title: No environment parity
findings.description: Development and production use the same hardcoded configuration. No environment-specific configuration or deployment stages.
evidence: Single web.config with hardcoded production credentials

findings.title: No AI/ML integration or readiness
findings.description: The application has no machine learning models, no AI-powered features, and no integration points for AI services.
evidence: No AI/ML libraries, SDKs, or service integrations in the codebase

findings.title: No structured data pipeline for ML training
findings.description: Timesheet data is locked in an operational database with no mechanism to extract, transform, or feed it into ML workflows.
evidence: No data export or ETL processes

securityFindings.detail: String concatenation used to build SQL queries from user/session input in Timesheet.aspx.vb
Database password (Time2006!) hardcoded in web.config committed to source control
Forms authentication configured with requireSSL=false, transmitting credentials over unencrypted connections
User inputs (date, hours, project) used directly in SQL statements with no sanitization
All platform components (OS, web server, framework, database) are end-of-life with no security patches

phase1.name: Replatform Foundation
steps: Rewrite to .NET 8+ ASP.NET Core Web API
Migrate to parameterized data access with Entity Framework Core

phase2.name: Cloud Infrastructure
steps: Secure credentials with AWS Secrets Manager

phase3.name: Operational Excellence
steps: Implement CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline
Deploy to Amazon ECS/EKS with auto-scaling
Add observability (structured logging, AWS X-Ray, CloudWatch)

phase4.name: Advanced Capabilities
steps: Add analytics integration with Amazon QuickSight
Enable AI capabilities with Amazon Bedrock integration
